text: Woe to the land of whirring wings, beyond the rivers of Cush,

which sends its envoys by sea, in vessels of papyrus over the waters. Go, swift messengers, to a nation tall and smooth-skinned, to a people feared far and wide, a nation mighty and conquering, whose land the rivers divide.
All you inhabitants of the world, all who dwell on the earth: when a banner is raised on the mountains, look; when the trumpet sounds, listen.
For this is what the LORD said to me: I will stay quiet and watch from my dwelling place, like shimmering heat in the blaze of noon, like a cloud of dew in the heat of harvest.
For before the harvest, when the blossom is over and the flower becomes a ripening grape, he will cut off the shoots with pruning knives and strip away the spreading branches.

versions.text: For before the harvest, when the blossom is gone and the flower has ripened into grapes, he will cut off the shoots with pruning knives and strip away the spreading branches.
versions.explanation: בֹּסֶר גֹּמֵל refers to grapes still ripening, not fruit already ripe; "has ripened into grapes" overstates the stage of growth and weakens the image of judgment falling just before maturity.

text: They will all be left to the mountain birds of prey and to the wild beasts of the land; the birds of prey will summer on them, and all the wild beasts will winter on them.

versions.text: They will all be left to the birds of prey of the mountains and to the beasts of the earth; the birds of prey will summer on them, and all the beasts of the earth will winter on them.
versions.explanation: "the birds of prey of the mountains" stacks two "of" phrases and stumbles when read aloud; "mountain birds of prey" flows better. Trimming the repeated "beasts of the earth" in the second clause also improves rhythm without losing meaning.

text: At that time gifts will be brought to the LORD of hosts by a people tall and smooth-skinned, from a people feared far and wide, a nation mighty and conquering, whose land the rivers divide — brought to the place of the name of the LORD of hosts, to Mount Zion.

versions.text: At that time gifts will be brought to the LORD of hosts from a people tall and smooth-skinned, from a people feared far and wide, a nation mighty and conquering, whose land the rivers divide — brought to the place of the name of the LORD of hosts, to Mount Zion.
versions.explanation: The first phrase (עַם מְמֻשָּׁךְ וּמוֹרָט) has no preposition in Hebrew and stands as the bringer of the gift, while the second phrase does carry מִן ("from"). Rendering the first as "by a people" preserves the distinction and avoids a flat repetition of "from... from...".
